correctedBuilderSelfSeal.reason: wp14_freeze_v2.py was derived from wp14_freeze.py, so its STATIC_REPOSITORY_FILES set still named the v1 builder and the v1 test. A freeze that does not seal its own builder would verify while its own source drifted freely, so v2 now seals wp14_freeze_v2.py and tests/test_wp14_freeze_v2.py. Pinned by Wp14FreezeV2SelfSealTests.test_the_receipt_seals_the_v2_builder_and_its_own_test.

divergences.endToEndProof: w14-d20181112-s10-r1-w17-b1-ref-s7, the job that halted the v1 matrix, was re-run standalone under the corrected mapper and completed: status pass, semanticHash cdef311b4d98c78c2eed9981c6bf274ab4fb668a9225c7c15e6cab7028e6dda5, 789.611 s wall.
divergences.reason: The mapper floored edge progress to permille and, at zero, reported the vehicle as standing on the node behind it. On a directed network that is not a conservative approximation but a different place: a vehicle cannot un-enter an edge. Measured on w14-d20181112-s10-r1-w17-b1-ref-s7, the first evening job of the v1 matrix: vehicle 4 sat at FleetPy position (86, 8, 0.000126) - 0.126 permille along edge 86->8 - and was reported to the core as node 86. The core costed 86->39 at 574.616 s; the true cost from the vehicle's position was 792.244 s, and reaching node 86 again costs 1352.586 s on its own. The 217.628 s gap turned 25.384 s of believed slack into a 192.244 s pickup-window violation that FleetPy rejected outright. Both engines agreed on travel times and deadlines to the millisecond; only the origin differed. The core was never wrong - RouteScheduleProjector already models an edge position by adding the remaining edge time and continuing from the to-node - it simply never received one. The corrected mapper keeps the vehicle on the edge and clamps to one permille, the smallest step EdgeProgressPermille admits and so the most conservative point the wire can express; exact-zero progress still maps to the from-node because the vehicle has not committed to the edge yet.
divergences.recoveryProof: The archived bytes were restored over the working file and the adapter package tree seal was recomputed with the freeze's own tree_sha256 under domain RideBound.Wp14AdapterPackage.v1. It reproduced f6c4db94711b8e16a0bde69ac7acf7e5abe9dfd835a213ddb91bfc713f6ca697 exactly, which is the value freeze v1 sealed. The corrected mapper was then restored.

divergences.reason: The runner hardcoded wp14_freeze.py and the v1 run-summary schema. A v2 receipt handed to the v1 builder fails with 'freeze receipt differs from its sources', which reads like corruption rather than a stale builder. Both the builder and the summary contract are now selected by the receipt's declared freeze identity; selection stays safe because the selected builder still rebuilds the whole receipt from source and compares it.

purpose: The freeze-receipt-v1 document seals the exact tree the WP14 development ablation was authorized against, including the adapter package as a single tree hash. The v1 matrix ran 40 of its 160 jobs cleanly and then halted on the first evening job with RBWP7_FLEETPY_PLAN_INFEASIBLE. The cause was a defect in that sealed adapter, so correcting it necessarily changes the sealed tree and freeze v1 can no longer be rebuilt from the working tree. The divergence is declared here with the frozen hashes and a location the frozen bytes are recoverable from, so the v1 provenance chain and its retained halt stay complete and auditable.
